flash.lead: Install, back up and restore over USB. Needs Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.start.title: What do you want to do?
flash.task.install.text: A first install, or an update.
flash.task.backup.text: Channels, settings and calibration, saved to a file.
flash.task.restore.text: From a backup file saved by this page.
flash.task.help.text: After an install that failed or went wrong.
flash.log.summary: This page reports which radio and firmware you install, restore or back up, and whether it worked, so we can find failures.
flash.log.sent: Sent: a random ID, the task, the radio model, the firmware version and features, and the result or error. Never your firmware files, backups or radio data.
flash.log.kept: Stored with your IP address. Custom build requests are stored the same way even with reporting off, to stop abuse. Never sold or shared.
flash.log.choices: Opt out with ?reporting=0, or --no-reporting in odrflash.
flash.log.contact: To see or delete your data, email
flash.start.privacy: Firmware comes from this site. Your stock firmware file, backups and radio data stay on your computer.
flash.support.none: This browser can't talk to radios. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.support.usb: This browser can't install firmware. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.support.serial: This browser can't talk to a radio running OpenDigitalRadio. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.sim.banner: Practice mode: the radio is simulated.
flash.sim.image: Practice mode uses a made-up firmware.
flash.sim.enter_bootloader: Practice: put the radio in update mode
flash.radio.title: Which radio do you have?
flash.radio.detect_hint: Already running OpenDigitalRadio? Plug it in, switch it on and let the page find it.
flash.build.title: Which features?
flash.build.lead: Full has everything this radio can run. Turn single features on or off below to get a custom build.
flash.build.unavailable: {error} You can also build it yourself (below).
flash.build.on_request: The firmware is prepared for you when you continue, usually in under a minute.
flash.build.version_on_request: Continue prepares version {ref} for you, usually in under a minute.
flash.version.title: Version {ref}.
flash.version.text: This link installs it instead of the latest release. Use it only if you were asked to try it.
flash.version.bad: This link asks for version "{ref}", which the page can't find. The link needs a release name (like v0.3.0) or a full commit hash (40 characters). Ask for a new link, or install the latest release.
flash.version.confirm_text: Version {ref} isn't the latest release, and it may have bugs that the release doesn't have. Only install it if you were asked to try it.
flash.version.confirm_back: You can go back to the latest release or to your backup at any time.
flash.build.no_image: No firmware yet. Go back one step.
flash.build.self_text: Build it with this command, then choose the file here.
flash.now.title: What's on the radio now?
flash.now.odr_text: Plug the radio in and switch it on. The page checks it.
flash.now.stock_text: What it came with from the factory.
flash.now.unknown_text: You'll need the stock firmware file.
flash.now.reading_codec: Saving the voice codec from the radio…
flash.now.which_version: Original firmware version, if you know it:
flash.now.stock_backup_later: This page can't back up the original firmware on this radio yet. After the install it saves your channels, settings and calibration. The install doesn't change those.
flash.now.stock_backup_planned: After the install, the page saves your channels, settings and calibration. The install doesn't change those.
flash.backup.lead: Saved as a file on your computer.
flash.backup.after_lead: The radio still holds your original channels and calibration. Save them now.
flash.backup.saved: Backup saved ({size} KB). Keep it somewhere safe.
flash.backup.incomplete: Some parts couldn't be read: {files}. The rest is saved.
flash.backup.note_after: Saved right after OpenDigitalRadio was installed over the original firmware, before anything else changed.
flash.backup.task_lead: Plug the radio in and switch it on with OpenDigitalRadio running.
flash.backup.add_stock: Also put my stock firmware file in the backup (so restore can put the original firmware back)
flash.backup.stock_none: This page can't back up a radio that still has its original firmware. Choose Install instead. It saves a backup right after the install.
flash.codec.title: Voice codec
flash.codec.lead: DMR voice needs the radio maker's voice codec. It isn't part of OpenDigitalRadio. It stays in the radio, or comes from your stock firmware file.
flash.codec.mode.keep: Keep the codec that's in the radio
flash.codec.mode.merge: Take the codec from my stock firmware file
flash.codec.key_from_radio: The radio's update key was read from the radio.
flash.codec.stock_unknown: not a stock firmware file this page knows
flash.write.title: Install
flash.write.bootloader_title: Put the radio in update mode
flash.win.title: Windows only: install the update-mode driver (once per computer)
flash.win.failed: On Windows this usually means the update-mode driver isn't installed yet. Install it, then try again:
flash.win.step1: Download Zadig and run it (it needs no install):
flash.win.step2: Put the radio in update mode (above) and plug it in.
flash.win.step3: In Zadig's list pick “{product}”. The USB ID boxes show {usb_id}. If it isn't listed, choose Options › List All Devices.
flash.win.step4: Choose WinUSB as the driver (right of the green arrow) and click Install Driver, or Replace Driver. Wait until Zadig says it succeeded.
flash.win.step5: Unplug the radio, put it back in update mode and try again.
flash.win.note: Only update mode needs this driver. Other tools that use the same USB device, such as the maker's upgrade tool or the MD-380's CPS, need their own driver back. To restore it, uninstall the device in Device Manager with “Delete the driver software”, then plug the radio in again.
flash.write.unexpected: The radio calls itself “{what}”, which doesn't match this model. Check you picked the right radio.
flash.write.failed: The install stopped ({error}). Put the radio in update mode and install again.
flash.f4.codec_text: This update goes over the cable and leaves the voice codec in the radio. It needs no stock file and no update mode.
flash.f4.title: Install
flash.f4.lead: Keep the radio on and plugged in until the page says it's done. The screen doesn't change during the install.
flash.f4.safety: If the install stops partway, the radio starts in update mode the next time you switch it on, and the install can finish there.
flash.f4.enter_failed: The radio didn't start the install: {error}. Nothing was changed. Use update mode below instead.
flash.f4.after_fail: If the radio doesn't answer any more, switch it off and on. It starts in update mode, and you can finish below.
flash.f4.repick: The radio reconnected under a new name. Pick it once more to go on.
flash.f4.kept: Part of the codec shares space with the firmware. A copy was saved as {file} first, and the codec is put back unchanged.
flash.f4.ok: Done and checked. The radio restarts now.
flash.f4.same: The radio already had this firmware. The radio restarts now.
flash.done.title: Check the radio
flash.done.lead: The radio restarts. When its screen is back, check that everything works.
flash.help.calm_text: This page never writes the part of the radio that runs update mode, so update mode still works. From there the radio can go back to OpenDigitalRadio, your backup or its original firmware.
flash.help.s.dark: It won't switch on, or the screen stays dark
flash.help.s.dark_text: No picture, or nothing happens at all.
flash.help.s.stuck: It switches on, but doesn't work right
flash.help.s.stuck_text: It freezes, restarts over and over, or shows something odd.
flash.help.s.stopped_text: An error, the cable came out, or the computer went to sleep.
flash.help.s.novoice: It works, but DMR voice doesn't
flash.help.s.novoice_text: FM works, digital calls are silent.
flash.help.s.channels: It works, but my channels are wrong
flash.help.s.channels_text: Channels, contacts or settings are missing or changed.
flash.help.s.revert: It works, I just want to go back
flash.help.s.revert_text: To my backup or to the original firmware.
flash.help.battery_text: A flat battery is the most common cause. Put on a charged battery, or charge this one for an hour, then switch the radio on.
flash.help.um_title: Put the radio in update mode
flash.help.um_lead: Update mode works even when the firmware is broken. Put the radio in update mode, and the page checks that it can reach it.
flash.help.um_not_found: The page didn't find the radio in update mode. Try these, then press Check again:
flash.help.hint_cable: Push the cable fully into the radio, and try another USB port.
flash.help.hint_keys: Hold the keys before you switch the radio on, and keep holding them until it's on.
flash.help.nohope_lead: The cause is usually the battery or the cable.
flash.help.nohope_battery: Charge the battery fully, or try another one.
flash.help.nohope_port: Try another cable or another computer if you have one.
flash.help.nohope_again: Then try update mode once more.
flash.help.ask: If none of this works, ask on the issue tracker:
flash.help.fix_title: How do you want to fix it?
flash.help.fine_title: The radio answered in update mode
flash.help.fine_text: Nothing is broken. Choose how to put it back.
flash.help.c7_reach: The page can reach the radio over the cable at power-on, even when the screen stays dark.
flash.help.fix.again_text: No files needed. Use this when an install stopped partway.
flash.help.fix.codec_text: You need your stock firmware file ({files}).
flash.help.fix.backup_text: You need the backup file this page saved (.zip).
flash.help.fix.backup_channels: You need the backup file this page saved (.zip). Only the channels and settings are put back.
flash.help.fix.stock_text: You need the stock firmware file ({files}).
flash.help.fix.stock_c7: You need the backup this page saved before the first install.
flash.help.fixed_text: If the problem comes back, open this help again.
flash.help.stock_done_text: The radio restarts with its original firmware. Channels and calibration weren't changed.
flash.done.ready: OpenDigitalRadio is running and DMR voice works.
flash.done.no_codec: The radio has no voice codec, so DMR voice doesn't work. FM does. Go back to the codec step and take the codec from your stock firmware file.
flash.restore.title: Choose your backup file
flash.restore.lead: The .zip file this page saved when you backed up.
flash.restore.to_odr_text: Firmware and codec as they were, then the channels and settings.
flash.restore.to_stock_text: The maker's firmware from your stock file, codec included.
flash.restore.stock_needed: Choose your stock firmware file. It holds the original firmware and the key that update mode needs.
flash.restore.done_stock: The radio restarts with its original firmware.
flash.restore.spi_note: Your channels and calibration weren't changed. To put your original channels back, use the maker's programming software.
flash.restore.codeplug_title: Put the channels and settings back
flash.restore.codeplug_lead: When the radio has restarted, connect it. The page compares its channels and settings with the backup and writes back what differs.
flash.restore.codeplug_refused: The radio protects some areas and refused {n} of {total} parts.
flash.err.load: The page didn't load completely. Reload it.
flash.err.security: The browser blocked USB. Open this page over https.
flash.err.no_serial: This browser can't talk to the radio. Use Chrome or Edge.
flash.err.no_usb: This browser can't install firmware. Use Chrome or Edge.
flash.err.no_answer: The radio didn't answer. Is it switched on and running OpenDigitalRadio? Close any other program that uses the radio.
flash.err.unknown_board: This page doesn't know the radio “{board}”.
flash.err.wrong_board: The radio says it is a {board}, not a {name}.
flash.err.not_in_bootloader: The radio isn't in update mode.
flash.err.need_stock_for_key: Choose your stock firmware file first. The page needs it to unlock update mode.
flash.err.stock_as_image: That's a stock firmware file, not an OpenDigitalRadio image.
flash.net.found: The radio is set to USB network mode, so the page can't talk to it.
flash.net.none: No radio found. Check the cable, and that the radio is on and running OpenDigitalRadio.
flash.net.step1: On the radio: Tools > USB network (OK, 5, 4), choose “Switch USB to serial”.
flash.net.step2: If Settings > Connections > USB network at start is on, turn it off, or the radio starts as a network adapter again.
home.codec: The AMBE voice codec isn't included. The installer keeps the one in your radio or takes it from your stock firmware file.
home.f_voice_text: DMR Tier II and FM. CTCSS/DCS, VOX, scan, dual watch, VFO.
home.f_data_text: Text messages, location (LRRP, ARS), emergency, call alert, radio check.
home.f_network_text: MMDVM hotspot, single frequency repeater, APRS. Over USB: status page, rigctld, SNMP, TFTP.
radio.note.dm1701: FM, DMR voice and data, text messages, the hotspot and the USB network services work on air.
radio.note.dm32: Not yet tested on a radio.
radio.note.md380: Not yet tested on a radio. No CTCSS/DCS yet.
radio.note.dm1801pro: Early bring-up. It boots on a radio; display, keys and storage work. FM and DMR are not yet checked on air, and DMR has no voice yet.
radio.note.db25d: Early work: FM receive only, no transmit or DMR yet. Not yet tested on a radio.
planned.note.tyt-md-uv380--md-uv390-rete: Same hardware family as the DM-1701. Next in line.
planned.note.tyt-md-9600-retevis-rt90: Mobile radio, same hardware family as the DM-1701.
planned.note.radioddity-gd-77-tyt-md-760: Needs a radio for development. A DM-1801 bought new today is not v1.
flash.backup.opt.all_text: Firmware, codec, calibration, codeplug and the rest of the memory chip, including the stock firmware's resources.
flash.backup.opt.firmware_text: The firmware memory (firmware and codec) and the factory calibration.
flash.backup.opt.codeplug_text: Channels, contacts, zones and settings, and the factory calibration.
flash.codec.need_key: The page needs it to unlock update mode.
flash.codec.need_codec: The codec comes from your stock firmware file.
flash.codec.key_saved: This browser remembers the radio's update key.
flash.codec.codec_from_radio: The codec was saved from the radio and checked. This browser keeps a copy, so an install that stops partway can still be finished.
flash.codec.codec_from_radio_unsaved: The codec was saved from the radio and checked. This browser can't keep a copy (for example in a private window), so if the install stops partway you'll need the stock firmware file.
flash.codec.codec_saved: The codec this browser saved from your radio earlier is put back.
flash.codec.or_connect: If the radio already runs OpenDigitalRadio, go back and pick that. The page then checks the codec in the radio.
flash.codec.anyway_text: To take the codec from your stock file anyway, choose the file, then pick “Take the codec from my stock firmware file” below.
flash.restore.to_codeplug_text: Channels, contacts and settings as backed up. The firmware stays as it is.
flash.build.untested: OpenDigitalRadio hasn't run on a {name} yet. Only for testers. Save a backup first and keep your stock firmware file.
flash.build.wrong_options: The firmware came back without {name}={value}. Try again.
flash.err.wrong_option: The radio says it is an {board}, so its {option} is {value}. Go back to the build step and pick that.
flash.sim.try_c7000: Practice with a DM-1801 Pro (original firmware)
radio.c7_step1: Connect the programming cable to the radio and to the computer.
radio.c7_step2: Open the flasher and choose the cable. A radio that already runs ODR is found without keys or switching it off.
radio.c7_step3: Otherwise switch the radio off, and on again when the page asks. Don't hold any keys. The screen stays dark and the LED on top blinks yellow while the radio is in update mode.
flash.c7.retry_safe: The part of the radio that runs update mode is never written, so you can always connect again.
flash.c7.retry_how: Try again. If the page can't reach the radio, switch it off, press Back, and switch it on when the page asks. A stopped install continues where it stopped.
flash.c7.bundle_note: program-memory.bin holds the radio's firmware and codec (1 MB). data-memory.bin holds the channels, contacts, settings and factory calibration (16 MB).
flash.c7.visual.cable: The radio can be on or off for now.
flash.c7.visual.cycle: Switch the radio off, then on again with the power knob.
flash.c7.visual.led_wait: LED: slow yellow blink. The radio is in update mode, waiting.
flash.c7.visual.led_busy: LED: fast yellow blink. Installing. Don't touch the radio or the cable.
flash.c7.visual.screen_off: Screen: dark, as expected in update mode.
flash.c7.visual.screen_loader: Screen: "PC Loader Connected". The keys do nothing until the radio restarts.
flash.c7.visual.screen_on: Screen: on. The radio runs normally.
flash.c7.connect.title: Connect your {name}
flash.c7.connect.step_cable: Plug the programming cable into the radio's speaker-mic socket and into this computer. Use a charged battery.
flash.c7.connect.step_choose: Press Choose the cable and pick it in the list the browser shows.
flash.c7.connect.which_port_text: Unplug the cable and plug it back in while the list is open. The entry that disappears and comes back is the cable. It's often called FTDI, CH340, CP210x or PL2303, "usbserial" on a Mac, or COM with a number on Windows.
flash.c7.connect.odr_loading: Switching the radio to update mode. Leave it as it is. The screen shows "PC Loader Connected" in a moment.
flash.c7.connect.odr_failed: The radio didn't switch to update mode by itself ({error}). Switch it off and on instead.
flash.c7.connect.odr_restart: The page restarts the radio to reach update mode. This takes a few seconds.
flash.c7.connect.odr_restart_failed: The restart didn't reach update mode. Switch the radio off and on instead:
flash.c7.connect.step_on: Switch it on again. The page is waiting and connects within a second.
flash.c7.connect.no_keys: Don't hold any keys. In update mode the screen stays dark and the LED on top blinks yellow slowly.
flash.c7.connect.hint_order: Switch it off and on once more. The page is listening now.
flash.c7.connect.hint_plug: Push the cable plug fully into the radio. A loose plug is the most common cause.
flash.c7.connect.hint_battery: Use a charged battery. On a weak battery the radio may not reach update mode.
flash.c7.connect.hint_ch340: Your cable has a CH340 chip. Some of these don't reach update mode. If the radio still isn't found, try a cable with an FTDI chip.
flash.c7.connect.no_rom: The radio didn't answer within three minutes.
flash.c7.connect.rom_found: The radio answered. Getting it ready…
flash.c7.connect.load_failed: Getting the radio ready failed ({error}). Switch it off and try again.
flash.c7.connect.found_stub: The radio is still in update mode from before.
flash.c7.connect.found_odr_stub: The radio is in update mode.
flash.c7.connect.found_rom: The radio is in update mode.
flash.c7.connect.led_rom: On the radio, the LED on top blinks yellow slowly and the screen is dark. Continuing…
flash.c7.connect.led_odr: On the radio, the screen shows "PC Loader Connected" and the LED on top blinks yellow slowly. Continuing…
flash.c7.connect.wrong_radio: This firmware is for the {name}, but the radio on the cable is a {other}. Nothing was written. Start over and pick the {other}.
flash.c7.check.title: Back up and check the radio
flash.c7.check.lead_first: Before the install, the page saves the radio's firmware memory. This backup is how you go back to the original firmware, and it holds the voice codec OpenDigitalRadio needs. It's downloaded and also kept in this browser.
flash.c7.check.lead_update: The radio runs OpenDigitalRadio, so the page only checks the codec, which takes a few seconds. You can also save a full backup.
flash.c7.check.only_copy: This backup is the only copy of your radio's original firmware.
flash.c7.check.only_copy_text: The maker doesn't offer this firmware for download. Keep the file in a safe place, such as a cloud folder or a USB stick. Without it, the radio can't go back to its original firmware.
flash.c7.check.opt_progmem_first: Needed before the first install. It holds the original firmware and its codec.
flash.c7.check.opt_q128_text: Channels, contacts, settings and the factory calibration. The page never changes these. A copy is still useful.
flash.c7.check.progmem_skipped: not needed (only the codec was read)
flash.c7.check.is_unknown: a firmware this page doesn't know (it's in your backup)
flash.c7.check.saved_both: downloaded and kept in this browser
flash.c7.check.saved_download: downloaded (this browser can't keep a copy, for example in a private window)
flash.c7.check.saved_slot: the codec is kept in this browser
flash.c7.codec.keep: The radio's codec is intact and stays.
flash.c7.codec.from_radio: The codec from the radio's original firmware (version {tag}) is carried over.
flash.c7.codec.from_browser: The codec this browser kept from this radio is carried over.
flash.c7.codec.from_file: The codec comes from your file {name}.
flash.c7.codec.none: No codec. FM works, DMR voice doesn't.
flash.c7.codec.action: DMR voice needs the radio's own codec
flash.c7.codec.action_text: The page found no codec it knows in the radio. Choose a firmware backup of this radio (program-memory.bin from an earlier backup) or a stock firmware file.
flash.c7.codec.pick: Choose a backup or stock file
flash.c7.codec.without: Install without the codec (FM only, add it later)
flash.c7.codec.none_risk: DMR voice stays off until you install again with a codec.
flash.c7.write.title: Install
flash.c7.write.careful: Leave the radio and the cable alone until the page says it's done.
flash.c7.write.careful_text: The LED blinks fast during the install. Only changed parts are written, and each one is checked. If the install stops, run it again.
flash.c7.write.ok: Done and checked. The radio restarts now.
flash.c7.write.lost: the radio doesn't answer any more
flash.c7.write.map_label: The radio's firmware memory, one square per part
flash.c7.done.lead: The page asks the radio what it runs, over the same cable.
flash.c7.done.ready: OpenDigitalRadio is running. FM and DMR voice work.
flash.c7.done.no_codec: OpenDigitalRadio is running without a codec, so DMR voice is off. Install again with a codec.
flash.c7.done.no_answer: The radio didn't answer yet. If its screen shows OpenDigitalRadio, it worked. Otherwise switch it off and on, and check again.
flash.c7.done.backup_kept: Keep the backup you downloaded. Restore, on the start page, uses it to put the original firmware back.
flash.c7.done.next_time: Next time you update, the radio goes into update mode by itself. You won't need to switch it off.
flash.c7.done.next_time_power: Next time, the page tries to put the radio into update mode by itself, and asks you to switch it off and on only if that doesn't work.
flash.c7.backup.lead: This works with any firmware on the radio. Every part is checked after it's read.
flash.c7.backup.progmem_text: 1 MB: the firmware and the codec.
flash.c7.backup.q128_text: 16 MB: channels, contacts, settings and the factory calibration.
flash.c7.restore.title: Put the firmware back
flash.c7.restore.lead: Writes the backup's firmware and codec back exactly. Only the parts that differ are written. The start-up area is never written.
flash.c7.restore.done: Done and checked. The radio restarts with the restored firmware.
flash.c7.restore.other_radio: This backup is from another radio model.
flash.c7.restore.data_note: The page doesn't write the data memory back. The radio keeps its current channels and settings.
